indicator.subject: Science
indicator.content_standard: B4.2.1.1 Recognise that some events in our environment occur recurrently
indicator.objective: Demonstrate understanding of cyclic movements in the environment

skills.description: Recognise that a movement or event that repeats in a regular pattern is called a cycle.
Identify examples of cyclic movements in the environment (e.g. swinging pendulum, clock hands, merry-go-round, walking limbs).
Describe the back-and-forth (to-and-fro) swinging of a pendulum as a cyclic movement.
Describe the repeating movement of the second hand on an analogue clock.
Describe how parts of the body move in a repeating pattern during walking.
State the common feature of cyclic movements (they repeat after a regular time or pattern).

spec.difficultyPlan: 20 questions total — Difficulty 1: 5; Difficulty 2: 7; Difficulty 3: 5; Difficulty 4: 3.
misconceptions: A cycle is any movement, even if it does not repeat.
A pendulum moves in only one direction.
Walking is not a cycle because we can stop.
Merry-go-round is not cyclic because it does not go back and forth.

questions.stem: What is a cyclic movement?
options: A movement that happens only once
A movement that changes direction randomly
A movement that repeats in a regular pattern
A movement that stops and never starts again
hints: Think about the word 'cycle' — like a bicycle wheel going round and round.
Does a cyclic movement happen once or many times?
questions.explanation: A cyclic movement is a movement that repeats in a regular pattern. The word 'cycle' means going round and round or repeating.
questions.misconception: A cycle is any movement, even if it does not repeat.

questions.stem: Which of these is a cyclic movement?
options: A swinging pendulum
A car moving from Accra to Kumasi
A stone falling once to the ground
A girl walking straight to the market and stopping
hints: Which movement keeps repeating?
A pendulum swings back and forth many times.
questions.explanation: A pendulum keeps swinging back and forth in a regular pattern. That is a cyclic movement.
questions.misconception: A cycle is any movement, even if it does not repeat.

questions.stem: What does the second hand of an analogue clock do?
options: It moves once and stops
It only moves when someone pushes it
It moves randomly in any direction
It moves round the clock face again and again
hints: Watch a clock for one minute.
Does the second hand keep moving?
questions.explanation: The second hand moves round the clock face again and again in a regular pattern. This is a cyclic movement.
questions.misconception: Clock hands move randomly.

questions.stem: A pendulum is a small ball hanging on a string. When you pull the ball to one side and let it go, what does it do?
options: It falls off the string
It swings back and forth
It stays still
It spins round and round
hints: Think about a swing in a playground.
It moves from one side to the other.
questions.explanation: When you let go, the ball swings from one side to the other and back again. This back-and-forth movement is cyclic.
questions.misconception: A pendulum moves in only one direction.

questions.stem: When you walk, your legs move in a pattern. What kind of pattern is this?
options: A random pattern
A pattern that happens only once
A pattern that repeats
A pattern that never repeats
hints: Think about the steps you take when walking.
Left, right, left, right — does the pattern repeat?
questions.explanation: When we walk, our legs move left, right, left, right in a repeating pattern. This repeating pattern makes walking a cyclic movement.
questions.misconception: Walking is not a cycle because we can stop.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes a cyclic movement?
options: It repeats after a regular time or pattern
It happens once and never again
It only happens at night
It never stops
hints: Think of the word 'cycle'.
Does it happen once or many times?
questions.explanation: A cyclic movement repeats after a regular time or pattern. Examples include a clock's second hand and a swinging pendulum.
questions.misconception: Cyclic movements never stop.

questions.stem: Which of these is NOT a cyclic movement?
options: A pendulum swinging
A merry-go-round turning
The hands of a clock moving
A ball rolling once down a hill
hints: Which movement happens only once and does not repeat by itself?
A ball rolling down a hill stops at the bottom.
questions.explanation: A ball rolling once down a hill does not repeat by itself. The other three movements repeat in a regular pattern.
questions.misconception: A cycle is any movement, even if it does not repeat.

questions.stem: Ama set up a pendulum and watched it. What describes the movement of the pendulum?
options: It moves forward and never comes back
It moves back and forth many times
It spins in a full circle
It moves only when touched
hints: Think about how a pendulum hangs.
Does it swing from side to side?
questions.explanation: A pendulum swings from one side to the other and back again, many times. This is a back-and-forth cyclic movement.
questions.misconception: A pendulum moves in only one direction.

questions.stem: Why is the movement of the second hand on an analogue clock called a cyclic movement?
options: Because it moves only when the clock is wound
Because it only moves during the day
Because it moves in a straight line
Because it goes round the clock face again and again
hints: Watch the second hand for one minute.
Does it return to where it started?
questions.explanation: The second hand goes round the clock face and returns to the same position again and again. This regular repeating is what makes it cyclic.
questions.misconception: Clock hands move randomly.

questions.stem: What is the common feature of a swinging pendulum, the second hand of a clock and a merry-go-round?
options: They all move in a repeating pattern
They all move in straight lines
They all stop after one round
They all only move at night
hints: Think about what happens after each movement.
Do they keep doing the same movement?
questions.explanation: All three movements repeat in a regular pattern. That is the common feature of cyclic movements.
questions.misconception: A cycle is any movement, even if it does not repeat.

questions.stem: Which of these is a cyclic movement?
options: A kite flying once across the sky
A boy running in a straight line
A merry-go-round in a playground
A stone thrown into a river
hints: Which one keeps going round and round?
A merry-go-round goes round again and again.
questions.explanation: A merry-go-round turns round and round, returning to the same position repeatedly. This is a cyclic movement.
questions.misconception: Merry-go-round is not cyclic because it does not go back and forth.

questions.stem: Name one movement of your body that is cyclic.
hints: Think of something you do again and again.
Walking uses your legs in a repeating pattern.
questions.explanation: Walking, breathing, blinking and chewing are all movements that repeat. They are cyclic movements of the body.
questions.misconception: Only machines show cyclic movement.

questions.stem: Pupil A says a pendulum is cyclic. Pupil B says a merry-go-round is cyclic. What makes both movements cyclic?
options: They both happen only once
They both happen again and again in a regular pattern
They both happen only at night
They both move very fast
hints: Think about what happens after one round.
Do they keep repeating?
questions.explanation: Both movements happen again and again in a regular pattern. Repeating regularly is what makes a movement cyclic.
questions.misconception: A cycle is any movement, even if it does not repeat.

questions.stem: A pupil notices that the sun rises every morning and sets every evening. Why is this a cyclic movement?
options: Because it happens every day in a regular pattern
Because it happens only in Kumasi
Because the sun moves in a straight line
Because the sun disappears forever
hints: Think about how often the sun rises.
Does it happen every day?
questions.explanation: The sun rises and sets every day in a regular pattern. This repeated daily pattern is a cycle.
questions.misconception: A cycle is any movement, even if it does not repeat.

questions.stem: Describe the movement of a pendulum in one sentence.
answer: a pendulum swings back and forth in a regular pattern
it swings from side to side and back again
hints: It is a ball on a string.
It moves from one side to the other and back.
questions.explanation: A pendulum swings from side to side and back again in a regular pattern. This back-and-forth movement repeats, so it is cyclic.
questions.misconception: A pendulum moves in only one direction.

questions.stem: A pupil watches the second hand of an analogue clock. The hand passes the 12 at 10:00:00 am and again at 10:01:00 am. What does this show?
options: The hand moves randomly
The hand stops after one round
The hand repeats its movement every 60 seconds
The hand only moves once a day
hints: How many seconds are in one minute?
Does the hand come back to the same place after 60 seconds?
questions.explanation: The second hand passes the 12 once every 60 seconds. So its movement repeats every 60 seconds in a regular pattern — that is a cycle.
questions.misconception: Clock hands move randomly.

questions.stem: A pupil lists movements they see at home. Which list contains ONLY cyclic movements?
options: A window being opened once, a door being closed once, a pot boiling
A cup falling off a table, a stone thrown into a river, a match being lit
A girl running to school, a boy jumping once, a goat eating once
A mother stirring soup round and round, a fan spinning, a child swinging on a swing
hints: Which list has movements that keep repeating?
Stirring, spinning and swinging all repeat.
questions.explanation: Stirring soup, a spinning fan and a child swinging all repeat in a regular pattern. The other lists contain one-time movements.
questions.misconception: A cycle is any movement, even if it does not repeat.

questions.stem: Explain why walking is a cyclic movement.
answer: because the legs move in a repeating pattern like left, right, left, right
because the legs keep moving in the same repeating pattern
because the legs keep alternating left and right in a pattern
hints: What pattern do your legs make when walking?
Does the pattern repeat?
questions.explanation: When we walk, our legs move left, right, left, right in a repeating pattern. This repeating pattern makes walking a cyclic movement.
questions.misconception: Walking is not a cycle because we can stop.

questions.stem: What do all cyclic movements have in common?
answer: they repeat in a regular pattern
hints: Think of the word 'cycle'.
Do they happen once or many times?
questions.explanation: All cyclic movements repeat in a regular pattern. A pendulum, a clock's second hand and a merry-go-round all do this.
questions.misconception: Cyclic movements never stop.

questions.stem: A pupil says, 'The movement of a fan is NOT cyclic because the fan can be switched off.' Is this correct?
options: Yes, because a movement must never stop to be cyclic
No, because a movement can stop and still be cyclic while it is happening
Yes, because only pendulums are cyclic
No, because a fan does not move
hints: Does stopping later mean the movement was never cyclic?
Think about the movement WHILE the fan is on.
questions.explanation: A cyclic movement can stop, but while it is happening, it repeats in a regular pattern. A fan blade turning round and round is cyclic while the fan is on.
questions.misconception: Cyclic movements never stop.
